confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: Stress is not phonemic in Toqabaqita, although there is potential for two compound words to be distinguished only by stress position; see further below for discussion. Stress assignment is governed by the following rules: I. The initial syllable of a word is stressed. There is one type of exception to this rule: when a monosyllabic grammatical morpheme cliticizes onto the following lexical word, …

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, left-anchored initial stress, final never stressed, no clash, no lapse of three, trisyllabic-foot defaults at n=5-6, rightmost stress marginally strongest) rests on the standard modern reference grammar by the language's principal linguist, and the deciding quotation was found verbatim at the stated page (p. 19) in a text-layer copy of that grammar; the worked examples on pp. 20-25 match the stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 10010 100100 1010100 (1 = a stressed syllable) (e.g. [úːusi] 100, [ùːusí-a] 1010, (2-46) ŋàlidaróʔa 10010 'not *10100', (2-45a) 100100 preferred over *101010, (2-50a) 1010100), and the fenced morphology-conditioned alternates (2-35f 10100; 2-35h, 2-47 101010) are also as printed. The held open-access dictionary (PL 592, p. 9) corroborates predictability and final-stress prominence. No better or instrumental source is listed in Glottolog or surfaced via Crossref. The

sources.quote: "Stress assignment is governed by the following rules: I. The initial syllable of a word is stressed. There is one type of exception to this rule: when a monosyllabic grammatical morpheme cliticizes onto the following lexical word, the stress is on the first syllable of the lexical element. ... II. The final syllable of a word is never stressed, except in cases of vowel elision (section 2.2.1). III. Neighbouring syllables cannot both be stressed, except in cases of vowel elision (section 2.2.1).
